title: Tax-Saving Investments under Section 80C, 80CCD: ELSS, PPF, and NPS
content:
For taxpayers opting for the Old Tax Regime in India, tax-saving instruments provide an opportunity to build long-term wealth while reducing annual tax liability. The primary statutory provisions are Section 80C and Section 80CCD of the Income Tax Act.

1. Section 80C (Maximum Deduction: ₹1,50,000):
Section 80C allows taxpayers to deduct up to ₹1.5 Lakhs from gross total income. Prominent qualifying vehicles include:
- Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS): ELSS is an equity-diversified mutual fund that invests predominantly in listed Indian equities. It features the shortest mandatory lock-in period among all 80C vehicles—just 3 years. Because ELSS invests in equities, it offers the highest long-term wealth creation potential, outperforming fixed-income alternatives over 5-to-10-year horizons.
- Public Provident Fund (PPF): PPF is a sovereign, guaranteed savings scheme offering 'EEE' (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) tax status: contributions are deductible under 80C, annual interest accrued is completely tax-exempt, and final maturity proceeds are 100% tax-free. PPF features a 15-year tenure with government-notified quarterly interest rates.
- Employees' Provident Fund (EPF): Mandatory retirement contribution (12% of basic salary) for organized sector employees, with guaranteed interest.

2. National Pension System (NPS - Section 80CCD):
NPS is a voluntary, market-linked retirement scheme managed by the PFRDA. It provides unique tax deductions:
- Section 80CCD(1): Covered within the overall ₹1.5 Lakh 80C limit.
- Section 80CCD(1B): An exclusive, additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 specifically for voluntary NPS contributions, over and above the ₹1.5L 80C ceiling.
- Corporate NPS (Section 80CCD(2)): Employer contributions up to 10% (14% for central government) of basic salary are deductible under both the Old and New Tax Regimes.
At age 60, up to 60% of the accumulated NPS corpus can be withdrawn tax-free as a lump sum, while the remaining 40% must be deployed into a monthly annuity.
